data.description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12: the declared non-goal is REVERSED. AI-assisted scheduling is now IN SCOPE and must ship tonight. Together with MRQ-149 this is the ENTIRE arithmetic distance from 98.7% to 100% on the eval.

RUBRIC ITEM: AIA-08, weight 1, type depth, testability auto. Currently `not_found` (zero credit).

CRITERION (verbatim): 'Some assisted or automatic scheduling capability exists that places unscheduled sessions into slots in one action ("AI" auto-scheduling judged generously as any auto-place assist).'

PASSES WHEN (verbatim): 'An auto-schedule/AI-assist control is present in the builder and, when triggered, places at least one previously unscheduled session into a slot/room. Judge generously -- any one-action assisted placement counts, and whether the result shows conflict flags is recorded but not gating. Fail if no such capability exists anywhere in the builder ... or if the control exists but performs no placement when triggered.'

READ THAT AGAIN, BECAUSE IT MAKES THIS TICKET SMALL: the rubric says 'judged generously' and 'any one-action assisted placement counts'. **You do not need an LLM. You do not need a model call. You do not need an optimiser.** A deterministic 'Auto-place' button that finds free time x room slots and assigns unscheduled sessions into them, in one action, EARNS THIS ITEM IN FULL. Do not build an AI scheduler tonight. Build an honest assisted placer.

MINIMUM BAR:
- A control in /agenda-builder (label it honestly -- 'Auto-place', 'Fill open slots', or similar).
- One click places at least one previously unscheduled session into a real slot and room.
- The placement persists across reload (it must go through the same path manual placement uses, not a client-side fake).
- Conflict flagging is recorded but NOT gating -- do not block the ship on perfect conflict avoidance. Prefer placing into non-conflicting slots where cheap, and let the existing conflict panel do its job otherwise.

BE HONEST IN THE COPY. PHILOSOPHY.md and this product's whole posture is that it does not overclaim. Do NOT label a deterministic placer as 'AI'. Call it what it is. The rubric explicitly accepts any assisted placement, so honesty costs nothing here -- and MRQ-146 exists precisely because the API was caught overclaiming. Do not create a second instance of that.

EVIDENCE THE JUDGE WANTS: screenshot of the control, plus before/after grid screenshots showing the previously unscheduled session now placed.

SIZE: small-to-medium, and it is worth more per hour than anything else left on the board.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, ai-agenda, AIA-08. Re-baseline by Eval Closer (surface:48) established this and MRQ-149 as the only remaining distance to 100%.
data.title: AIA-08: one-action assisted placement in the agenda builder

data.body:
Browser validation, real Worker via npx vite dev on the seeded AIE NYC 2026 demo (localhost:5251, organizer demo persona), c11 embedded browser.

CONTROL: 'Auto-place' button present in the /agenda-builder toolbar, between the Track filter and the status note. Tooltip: 'Fill open room and time slots with unscheduled Sessions. Deterministic, not AI — it seats what fits and leaves the judgement to you.' No 'AI' claim anywhere in the feature or its copy.

ONE CLICK, MEASURED:
  unscheduled pool   36 -> 16
  scheduled sessions 25 -> 45
  conflicts           7 ->  7 (the pass introduced none)
  notice: 'Auto-placed 20 Sessions into open slots · 16 still unscheduled · review and adjust'

PERSISTENCE proven twice, independently of client state:
  1. Fresh GET /api/v1/events/evt_aie-ny-2026/agenda returns sessions=45, unscheduled=16. Sample: 'Advanced AI Engineering with AI SDK' -> Central Park Ballroom, 2026-10-12T13:00Z, 90m.
  2. Full browser reload: all 20 render in the grid at real times and rooms; the publication panel's not-yet-public count went 1 -> 21.

Placements go through POST /agenda/items — the same route a manual drag uses. No new endpoint, no schema change.

EVIDENCE: docs/evidence/mrq-148/before-auto-place.png (control + pool of 36 + mostly empty grid), docs/evidence/mrq-148/after-auto-place-reloaded.png (post-reload grid filled, pool 16).

GATE (local): tsc --noEmit clean; vite build ok; check:design pass; check:api pass; trace:ac pass; npm test 187/187 pass (pass-over-budget, 173s vs 45s objective — box at load 41->82 on 16 cores, every assertion green); npm run pr-gate PASS at 95s of a 120s budget.

REGRESSION TEST: tests/unit/auto-place.MRQ-148.test.ts, 8 tests. Fails before — verified by running the suite against the pre-change source, module not found — and passes after.

PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/135

VALIDATION (live browser, real Worker): control present in /agenda-builder toolbar; one click placed 20 previously-unscheduled Sessions into real slot+room pairs; pool 36->16, sessions 25->45, conflicts unchanged at 7; all 20 survive a full page reload and a fresh server-side GET. Local gate green: tsc, vite build, check:design, check:api, trace:ac, pr-gate PASS (95s/120s), npm test 187/187. Screenshots at docs/evidence/mrq-148/. AIA-08 pass criteria met: an assist control exists and performs real placement when triggered.

MERGED AND VERIFIED ON MAIN.

PR #135 was reviewed by the Eval Fix Orchestrator (non-author read of the diff, posted as a comment because the fleet shares one GitHub account and a formal approval would be refused as self-review) and squash-merged at 2026-08-12T21:59:50Z. CI fast-gate on the PR: SUCCESS.

Independently verified after the c11 restart:
- Squash produced a new sha, so I compared content rather than ancestry: git diff aa4c33f9 github/main across src/lib/auto-place.ts, src/ui/agenda/AgendaPage.tsx, src/ui/agenda/agenda.css, tests/unit/auto-place.MRQ-148.test.ts is EMPTY. Byte-identical.
- The control is live on main: AgendaPage imports the planner, holds autoPlaceBusy, and renders the button with class agenda-auto-place / data-auto-place.
- CI on main has completed green twice since the merge (runs 31647135065, 31647483612).

COLLISION WITH MRQ-141 / PR #145: resolved, nothing owed by this ticket.
- #145 head eb6622e4 already contains MRQ-148 (12 autoPlace references) — they took main after the merge.
- git merge-tree against current main: zero conflicts.
- Inspected the merged tree b8d0b165 directly: Auto-place survives intact (AgendaPage 1100-1107 — class, data hook, 'Deterministic, not AI' tooltip, busy-label swap); the lib and the 8-test file are present.

ONE HANDOFF, for MRQ-157 (15-minute grid increments), flagged to the orchestrator at surface:47: autoPlaceSlots() derives its candidate openings from TIME_SLOTS in track-board.tsx, so Auto-place inherits a finer grid for free. But the test 'CONTRACT · slots come from the conference's own days and grid times, in board order' asserts the hourly shape (24 slots over two days, built[12] at day-two 09:00) and will go red on a 15-minute grid. That is an expectation update for whoever lands MRQ-157, not a defect in either feature.

REVIEW OF RECORD (transcribed, not authored by me — the reviewer is the Eval Fix Orchestrator, a non-author agent, posted on PR #135 at 2026-08-12T21:59:50Z and available in full at https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/135#issuecomment-5273273124):

- planAutoPlacements is honest deterministic arithmetic — room-busy and person-busy interval indexes built from existing sessions, half-open overlap test, pool consumed in board order. The same snapshot always yields the same plan, as the doc comment claims.
- Placements go through the ordinary POST /agenda/items route a drag uses, so the result is indistinguishable from hand-placed work. No new endpoint, no schema change — that is what makes the reload persistence real rather than optimistic.
- The partial-failure path is correct: placed is counted per successful write and the summary is rebuilt from placements.slice(0, placed), so a stop mid-pass reports what actually landed, not what was planned.
- Copy clears the honesty bar the project set for itself after MRQ-146 — the control's own tooltip says 'Deterministic, not AI', and a test asserts the summary never claims a model did the work.
- Craft rule respected: .agenda-auto-place carries a fixed min-width so the swap to 'Placing…' cannot shift the toolbar. Elements never jump.
- All eight test titles carry 'CONTRACT · '; trace:ac and CI fast-gate green. No secrets, no scope creep — one lib, one handler, one button, one CSS line.

Verdict: merged. No findings raised, so nothing was left to resolve.
